\begin{proposition}[Three prices on the same star]\label{prop:star}
For fixed $q,c,\gamma,f$, under the common original-cap certificate in
Appendix~\ref{app:star}, the universal-first order has
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{early reports, immediate allocation:}&
 V_I(\delta)\sim a\ell_2(1/\delta),\\
\text{early reports, retained allocation:}&
 V_{\mathrm{ER}}(\delta)\sim a\ell_{q+1}(1/\delta),\\
\text{late reports, retained allocation:}&
 V_{\mathrm{LR}}(\delta)\sim a\log(1/\delta).
\end{array}
\]
With the singletons first, the two early-report values both have leading
asymptotic $a\ell_{q+1}(1/\delta)$; the late-report price is unchanged.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial exact laminar strategy]
\label{thm:laminar}
Consider the current-window tool game with known stage order and a
laminar compatibility family.  For $q>0$, its suffixes admit a table of
normalized integer capacity vectors on the single tree $\mathcal L$
that determines $\rho(i,R)$ for every stage $i$ and every remaining-tool
set $R\subseteq U$.  The same table supplies a causal choice attaining
\[
 \max_{r\in S_i\cap R}\rho(i+1,R\setminus\{r\})
\]
whenever $S_i\cap R\ne\varnothing$.

Given the tree, the table uses
$O((N+1)(q+1)t)$ elementary integer operations and
$O((N+1)(q+1)t\log(q+2))$ bits of capacity storage.
Each rank query and each maximizing-tool query uses
$O((q+1)t)$ operations.  All capacities and counts lie in $[0,q]$.
For $N,q\ge1$, these bounds are respectively $O(Nqt)$ preprocessing
and $O(qt)$ per query.  From an explicit stage--tool incidence input,
the tree can first be constructed, and laminarity checked, in
$O((N+q+1)^2q)$ elementary set-membership operations.

If $q=0$, no tree is required: the rank is $1$ whenever a stage remains
and is $\infty$ at the terminal state.  In particular, the result does
not assume that a compact strategy is supplied as part of the input.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-graph price law]\label{thm:price}
Under the native freshness, reporting, correction, and charging assumptions,
suppose the original contract passes the rational resource certificate in
Section~\ref{subsec:price-native}.  If $d=\rho(1,U)<\infty$, the infimum
$V_I(\delta)$ of expected actual observation and correction charges satisfies
\[
 V_I(\delta)=C(1,U)\ell_d(1/\delta)(1+o(1)),
 \qquad C(1,U)>0.
\]
For any fixed initial remaining set $R$ of finite rank $d$, its coefficient
has the ordered expression
\begin{equation}
 C(1,R)=\sum_{i=1}^N A_i\ind\{b_i=d-1\},\qquad
 b_i=\begin{cases}
 0,&S_i\cap R=\varnothing,\\
 \max_{r\in S_i\cap R}\rho(i+1,R\setminus\{r\}),&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:price-head}
\end{equation}
If the initial rank is infinite, zero observations suffice and the actual
correction bill remains bounded.  The asymptotic statement is pointwise for
each fixed graph and channel instance; it is not uniform when $q,N$, or the
prices vary with $\delta$. The lower-bound direction requires no
sufficient resource certificate; that certificate is used for the
matching executable upper bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[A compact leading-price controller]
\label{cor:computable-price}
For laminar compatibility, the combinatorial preprocessing in
Theorem~\ref{thm:laminar} computes the depth and the critical stage
indices in~\eqref{eq:price-head} in polynomial time. It therefore returns
the exact symbolic expression for the leading coefficient in terms of
the supplied channel probabilities, as in Theorem~\ref{thm:price}; no
exact real-valued KL oracle is required. Replacing the generic subset oracle by the
capacity table implements its causal upper controller without
exponential tool-state expansion, under exactly the original resource
certificate in~\eqref{eq:price-rational-quota}--\eqref{eq:price-total-cap}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Closure on one tree]
\label{lem:laminar-closure}
The following operations preserve normalized capacity representations,
with $\mathsf{VOID}$ allowed, and cost $O(t)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For normalized $c$ and nonempty $S\in\mathcal L$, the family
$\mathcal E_S(\mathcal I(c))$ is obtained by decreasing $c_T$ by one
for every $T\in\mathcal A(S)$.  If any of these capacities was zero,
the result is $\mathsf{VOID}$; otherwise the resulting vector is already
normalized.
\item The intersection of two capacity families is represented by the
coordinatewise minimum of their vectors, followed by normalization.
\end{enumerate}
Also $\mathcal E_\varnothing(\mathcal I)=\mathsf{VOID}$,
$\mathcal E_S(\mathsf{VOID})=\mathsf{VOID}$, and an intersection with
$\mathsf{VOID}$ is $\mathsf{VOID}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Local logarithmic price]\label{lem:price-local}
For the fixed stage-$i$ experiment,
\[
 J_i(t)=A_i\log t\,(1+o(1))\quad(t\to\infty),\qquad
 0\le J_i(t)\le t.
\]
Moreover $J_i(t)=O_i(\log(1+t))$ for all $t\ge0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Full-history penalty bridge]\label{lem:price-bridge}
From every healthy native history at the first entry to stage $i$, with unused tools $R$, every legal policy satisfies
\[
 \E[\text{future actual observation charges}]
 +\lambda\Prob(\text{eventual task failure})\ge G_{i,R}(\lambda).
\]
This includes policies that delay an already allocated correction, abandon
before a write, or continue to incur charges after permanent failure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{remark}[Normal charges]\label{rem:price-normal-charges}
If a completed run incurs an additional fixed normal charge $C_0$, any
$\delta$-safe policy pays it on an event of probability at least $1-\delta$.
Thus its total-cost lower bound adds $(1-\delta)C_0$, and the constructed
upper bound adds at most $C_0$.  These are real charges, as are all fixed
correction prices.  Neither changes the divergent leading terms.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Fixed shared pool with a growing correction price]
\label{cor:fixed-pool-price}
Fix integers $N\ge1$, $0\le K<N$ and rational $c>0$,
$0<\gamma\le1/4$.  In the shared-pool $I_{\rm pay}$ model, consider
original contracts satisfying \eqref{eq:joint-certificate} as
$\delta\downarrow0$.  For any nonnegative rational price
$f=f(\delta)$, put
\[
 B_\delta=a(N-K)\ell_{K+1}(1/\delta),\qquad
 T_B=\min\{B_\delta+aN\log(1+f/a),\ aN\log(1+N/\delta)\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \frac{1-o(1)}{129}\,T_B
 \ \le\ V_f^{\rm nat}(\delta)\ \le\ 72(1+o(1))\,T_B.
\]
The $o(1)$ is independent of $f$ and of the choice of qualified native
caps, but may depend on the fixed $N,K,c,\gamma$.  In particular
$V_f^{\rm nat}(\delta)\asymp T_B$.  This is a small-risk statement for
a fixed pool, not an all-parameter uniform frontier or a sharp leading
coefficient for growing $f$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Exact randomized local ROC]
\label{lem:paid:roc}
The minimum expected review charge of a MAP experiment with average error
exactly $p\in(0,1/2]$ is $g(p)$.  The minimum for an arbitrary binary
decision of error $e\in(0,1)$ is
$\widetilde g(e)=g(\min\{e,1-e\})$.
Each $g(p)$ is attained by randomizing two adjacent symmetric likelihood
boundary tests.  For rational $p,c,\gamma$, their probabilities and mean
charges are rational and explicitly computable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Record-level representation]
\label{lem:paid:representation}
In the cap-relaxed model, every finite-cost full-history policy is first
dominated by the policy that stops at permanent failure.  This dominated
policy can be simulated by symmetric integer boundary experiments and
private auxiliary records, preserving its virtual write-error,
correction, and abandonment history law up to termination, with no greater
expected review charge.  Conditional on an auxiliary writing record of
posterior level $m$, its mean review charge is $\mathsf C_m$, and its decision
error is either $p_m$ or $1-p_m$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A uniformly attainable local bound]
\label{lem:paid:surrogate}
For $0<p\le1/2$, put
\[
 \psi(p)=\max\{a\phi(p),(c/\gamma)(1/2-p)\}.
\]
Then $\psi(p)\le g(p)\le4\psi(p)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Native eight-factor algorithm]
\label{thm:paid:native-eight}
The numbers in \eqref{eq:paid:certificate-numbers} and an explicit rational
algorithm satisfy \eqref{eq:paid:algorithm-sandwich} under
\eqref{eq:paid:cap-certificate}.  The output is an initial mixture of at most
two finite-state policies and bounded calibrated local tests.
\end{theorem}

sequential decisions, but their compatibility and allocation deadlines
matter as much as their number. We study a known sequence of outputs

\section{Introduction}
A correction can restore today's output while consuming the only means
of restoring tomorrow's. A snapshot, a version-bound correction handle
or a specialized recovery tool may work for some outputs and not others.
Even when all compatibilities are known, deciding which right to consume
requires a causal strategy. Counting unused tools or computing an
offline matching does not settle that decision.
source_dispositions.summary: Causal allocation motivation and offline-versus-online bottleneck

source_dispositions.text:
We study a precise abstraction: required outputs arrive in a known order,
evidence can be purchased before an output is fixed, and an exact report
then reveals whether it needs correction. Each reliable correction uses
one compatible tool once. The objective is to make every final output
correct with probability at least $1-\delta$ while minimizing expected
actual charges, including charges on failed runs. The structural core
asks which compatibility patterns permit compact exact causal planning.
source_dispositions.summary: Original abstraction and all-path expected actual fee objective

\subsection{A small example exposes two different bottlenecks}
Let there be $q\ge2$ tools and $q+1$ stages, with
\begin{equation}
 U=\{1,\ldots,q\},\qquad S_1=U,\qquad S_{j+1}=\{j\}\quad(1\le j\le q).
 \label{eq:example-star}
\end{equation}
The first output accepts any tool; each later output has its own tool.
These sets are laminar: intersecting sets are nested. Offline, every
set of at most $q$ errors is repairable. Online, if the first output is
wrong, consuming tool $j$ leaves singleton stage $j+1$ exposed. An
adaptive adversary can force failure with just two errors. With the
singletons first, their own tools repair them and an unused tool remains
for the last universal stage whenever at most $q$ errors occur. Thus
the order changes causal safety without changing offline matchability.
source_dispositions.summary: Two original star orders, offline matching and actual causal rank separation

\label{sec:model}

source_dispositions.text:
There are $N$ required output slots and a set $U$ of $q$ one-use tools.
The complete stage order and compatibility sets $S_i\subseteq U$ are
known. An erroneous output at stage $i$ can be genuinely corrected only
with a previously unused tool $r\in S_i$. Such a correction guarantees
the required value, consumes $r$, changes no other output and supplies
no additional hidden-state information.
source_dispositions.summary: Original correction rights and information/cross-output restrictions

source_dispositions.text:
At stage $i$, a fresh binary fact $X_i$ has a known nondegenerate prior
$\pi_i$. A review costs $c_i>0$ and has distribution $P_i^x$ on a
finite alphabet when $X_i=x$. The two distributions are distinct and
have full support. Conditional on every history generated before the
stage is entered, the same prior and iid observation kernel apply;
old history does not reveal the current observation tape. The next
fact and its review port are inaccessible until its stage opens.
All finite probabilities and fees are supplied rational inputs.
source_dispositions.summary: Fresh finite rational observation model, prior, hidden future ports and tapes

source_dispositions.text:
An ordinary write fixes a selected bit and closes that slot's ordinary
write and review ports. Its authoritative report reveals the true bit
and, if needed, a version-bound mismatch handle. A correction requires
this actual handle; a blind guaranteed overwrite is not native. In
early-report workflows the report arrives before the next fact is
born. A late-report workflow receives all reports after all ordinary
writes; advance depends on the write, so delay causes no deadlock.
source_dispositions.summary: Ordinary writes, genuine serial handles, early/late reports and advance

source_dispositions.text:
The current-window contract $I$ requires an erroneous output's tool
allocation to be irrevocable before advancing. A contract may also
require actual execution before advance. Our upper controllers execute
immediately, and the lower comparison permits the larger class in
which an already committed correction may be executed later. No such
tool can be reassigned. The retained contract $R$ instead keeps all
correction handles until a common terminal barrier and permits tools
to be assigned there. Original per-stage review quotas and a cumulative
call cap $H$ apply. There are no additional order-sensitive locks,
changing prices, cross-output effects or ways to reopen a review port.
source_dispositions.summary: Current/retained allocation, execution deadlines and original caps

source_dispositions.text:
Success means that all $N$ required final outputs are truly correct.
Abandonment, incomplete execution and unrepaired errors are failures.
A policy may use all visible history and private randomness, write
non-MAP values, decline corrections, delay where legal, and continue
spending after failure. Only the global condition
$\Prob(\mathrm{failure})\le\delta$ is imposed. If actual correction
$i,r$ costs a fixed $f_{ir}\ge0$, the variable bill is
\[
 C=\sum_i c_iT_i+\sum_{\text{actual corrections }(i,r)}f_{ir}.
\]
All failed-path charges count. Write $f_{\max}=\max f_{ir}$, or zero
when there is no compatible pair. Every policy uses at most
$\min(N,q)$ genuine corrections. Normal full-run fees $C_0$ are
accounted for separately; every successful run pays at least $C_0$,
and each constructed run pays at most $C_0$ in normal charges. Let
$H_0$ bound its normal calls on a complete execution. Local planning
work is reported as computation, separately from native calls.
source_dispositions.summary: Full randomized comparator, actual failure/nonreturn fees, C0 and selected complete-H0

\paragraph{The structural game.}
At a healthy state $(i,R)$, tools in $R$ are unused and all earlier
required allocations are resolved. An error adversary chooses either
to declare the current stage correct or to declare an error. An error
costs the adversary one unit; the allocator observes it and chooses
$r\in S_i\cap R$, irrevocably consuming $r$. If no such tool exists,
the adversary has forced failure. Future declarations can depend on
the realized allocations. The value $\rho(i,R)$ is the smallest error
budget that forces failure against an optimal causal allocator, or
$\infty$ if this is impossible. Healthy termination has value $\infty$.
The abstract adversary defines a structural parameter; it does not
replace the independent facts in the statistical model.

Equivalently, $\rho(i,R)>k$ means that some allocator handles every
adaptive pattern of at most $k$ future errors. Backward induction
permits pure Markov strategies for this finite game. The statistical

\section{A compact exact strategy for laminar compatibility}
\label{sec:laminar}

The compatibility family is \emph{laminar} if any two distinct nonempty
sets in $\{S_1,\ldots,S_N\}$ are either disjoint or one contains the
other.  Their temporal order is unrestricted, and the same set may occur
at several stages.  Throughout this section allocation is irrevocable:
an erroneous stage must receive an unused compatible tool before its
window closes.  The adversary may observe the realized allocation before
choosing subsequent errors.
source_dispositions.summary: Original laminar and adaptive irreversible allocation input

source_dispositions.text:
For $q>0$, augment the distinct nonempty compatibility sets by $U$ and
all singletons $\{r\}$, $r\in U$.  The resulting family $\mathcal L$
is still laminar.  Its inclusion tree has top node $U$ and singleton
leaves.  The children of every internal node partition that node.  Write
$t=|\mathcal L|$; in particular,
\[
 t\le N+q+1.
\]
Empty stage sets are not tree nodes and will be handled explicitly.
For a nonempty node $S$, let $\mathcal A(S)$ denote the path consisting
of $S$ and all its ancestors, including $U$.
source_dispositions.summary: Universe/singletons/tree/children/t bound, empty sets and ancestor path

\paragraph{Why the representation survives every stage.}
Let $D$ be the used-tool set.  A vector $b=(b_T:T\in\mathcal L)$
represents the downward-closed family
\[
 \mathcal I(b)=\{D\subseteq U:|D\cap T|\le b_T\text{ for all }T\in\mathcal L\}.
\]
Normalize bottom-up by replacing an internal capacity by the minimum of
itself and the sum of its children's capacities.  This preserves the
family because the children partition their parent.  Keep a separate
$\mathsf{VOID}$ symbol: zero capacities represent $\{\varnothing\}$,
which is not the empty family.
source_dispositions.summary: Capacity family/normalization/VOID distinction

source_dispositions.text:
For a normalized vector, a used set $D$ can be extended by some unused
tool in $S$ precisely when $D\in\mathcal I(b)$ and every node from $S$
to the root has one unit of slack.  Necessity follows because any chosen
tool increments all these counts.  For sufficiency, a slack internal node
has a slack child: its used count is the sum of its children's counts,
whereas its capacity is at most their capacity sum.  Descend from $S$
through slack children to an unused singleton.  This produces the tool,
not merely a yes/no feasibility answer.
source_dispositions.summary: Extension iff all ancestors slack and actual descent

source_dispositions.text:
Thus the extension operation $\mathcal E_S$ decrements capacities along
the $S$-to-root path.  A zero capacity on that path yields $\mathsf{VOID}$.
Intersection takes coordinatewise minima and normalizes.  Crucially,
both operations stay on the same tree.  Arbitrary matroid intersections
would not provide this representation.
source_dispositions.summary: Same-tree decrement/intersection/normalization closure
source_dispositions.notes: General matroid-intersection contrast is explanatory, not a separately claimed universal negative theorem.

source_dispositions.text:
\paragraph{The order-sensitive invariant.}
Let $\mathcal I_{i,k}$ consist of used sets from which the allocator
can handle every adaptive pattern of at most $k$ errors in suffix $i$.
With $\mathcal I_{i,0}=\mathcal I_{N+1,k}=2^U$, the exact recurrence is
\[
 \mathcal I_{i,k}=\mathcal I_{i+1,k}
       \cap\mathcal E_{S_i}(\mathcal I_{i+1,k-1})\qquad(k>0).
\]
The first branch preserves the error budget; in the second, the adversary
spends one error before the allocator chooses a tool.  Future declarations
may observe that choice.  Hence this is an online safety invariant, not
an offline test on a preselected error set.  The two closure operations
prove inductively that every entry is a capacity vector or $\mathsf{VOID}$.
source_dispositions.summary: Independent adaptive safety invariant and exact backward recurrence

source_dispositions.text:
Only budgets $0,\ldots,q+1$ are needed: each repair consumes a new tool,
so any finite rank is at most $q+1$.  Membership recovers
$\rho(i,R)=\min\{k:U\setminus R\notin\mathcal I_{i,k}\}$, with an
empty minimum equal to infinity.  To select an actual tool, scan the
suffix-budget entries for the greatest rank achievable by extension,
then run the slack-child descent in the last feasible entry.  It returns
a compatible tool maximizing the erroneous successor rank.
Appendix~\ref{app:laminar} gives the complete closure, extraction and
complexity proofs, including empty eligibility sets and zero tools.
source_dispositions.summary: Finite budget scan, exact maximal child and compact query

\label{sec:prices}

source_dispositions.text:
This section proves the statistical interface used by the laminar algorithm.
The compatibility graph, stage order, priors, channels, observation prices,
and correction prices are fixed.  Only the required risk $\delta$ and the
native resource contracts passing the sufficient test below may vary.
All logarithms in asymptotic expressions are natural.  Write
\[
 D_{ix}=\KL(P_i^x\Vert P_i^{1-x}),\qquad
 A_i=c_i\sum_{x=0}^1\frac{\pi_i(x)}{D_{ix}},\qquad
 \ell_1(z)=\log z,\quad \ell_{j+1}(z)=\log\ell_j(z).
\]
The fixed, finite, full-support channels are distinct, so $A_i>0$.
We retain the full policy comparator: visible-history dependence, private
randomness, non-MAP writes, legal delay, abandonment, refusal to correct,
and continued spending after failure are all allowed.  The only risk
constraint is the probability of failure of the entire required task.
source_dispositions.summary: Fixed input before risk/caps, exact coefficient and full comparator

 \qquad C(1,U)>0.
\]
For any fixed initial remaining set $R$ of finite rank $d$, its coefficient
has the ordered expression
\begin{equation}
 C(1,R)=\sum_{i=1}^N A_i\ind\{b_i=d-1\},\qquad
 b_i=\begin{cases}
 0,&S_i\cap R=\varnothing,\\
 \max_{r\in S_i\cap R}\rho(i+1,R\setminus\{r\}),&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:price-head}
\end{equation}
If the initial rank is infinite, zero observations suffice and the actual
correction bill remains bounded.  The asymptotic statement is pointwise for
each fixed graph and channel instance; it is not uniform when $q,N$, or the
prices vary with $\delta$. The lower-bound direction requires no
sufficient resource certificate; that certificate is used for the
matching executable upper bound.
\end{theorem}
source_dispositions.summary: Fixed-graph price including arbitrary initial R coefficient, infinity case and lower/upper qualification split

source_dispositions.text:
\paragraph{Why an allocation rank becomes a statistical depth.}
For a fresh fact, the best observation cost plus error penalty $z$ is
$J_i(z)\sim A_i\log z$.  Drop the caps and correction fees only for a
lower bound, and charge one penalty $\lambda$ for the entire task's
failure.  At a healthy state its exact value has the form
\[
 G_{i,R}=\min\{\lambda,\ G_g+J_i(G_b-G_g)\},
\]
where $G_g$ is the correct continuation and $G_b$ the cheapest legal
error continuation (or $\lambda$ if no repair is possible).
An additional error that the allocator can survive adds one logarithmic
layer.  When the correct and error successors have equal rank, their
leading terms may cancel inside $G_b-G_g$; the proof avoids a false
lower bound on this difference and uses
$0\le J_i(G_b-G_g)\le O_i(\log(1+G_b))$ instead.
The correct continuation then supplies the leading term.

This penalty argument is conditional on the visible past before the
fresh fact is born.  It never conditions stopped information on eventual
success.  It covers non-MAP writes and abandonment by filling only an
abandoned current decision for the lower-bound comparison.  Matching
controllers allocate a rational risk budget between the two branches,
test to posterior-error targets, and execute actual repairs immediately.
Explicit rational quotas truncate the ideal tests; overflow consumes part
of the original risk allowance and deletes only future nonnegative costs.
The entire derivation and the original-cap certificate appear in
Appendix~\ref{app:prices}; insufficient caps are not enlarged.
source_dispositions.summary: Penalty explanation, cancellation, actual controller and overflow fees

\subsection{Early reports with retained correction ports}

Let $M$ be the transversal matroid on the stage indices: a set of stages is
independent exactly when it can be matched to distinct compatible tools.
With early reports and ports retained until a common final barrier, retain
the discovered error set $H$ instead of committing tools early.  Define
\[
 g=\min\{|C|:C\text{ is a circuit of }M\},\qquad
 \mathcal H_g=\{\min C:C\text{ is a circuit of size }g\}.
\]
The minimum over no circuits is infinite.

\begin{corollary}[Retained-port girth and circuit heads]\label{thm:retained}
For early reports and retained ports, if $g<\infty$, then under the native rational resource certificate in
Section~\ref{subsec:price-native},
\begin{equation}
 V_{R,\mathrm{early}}(\delta)
 =\left(\sum_{i\in\mathcal H_g}A_i\right)
   \ell_g(1/\delta)(1+o(1)).
 \label{eq:price-retained}
\end{equation}
If $g=\infty$, zero observations suffice, with all actual correction and
normal charges retained. The lower-bound direction does not require the
sufficient quota test. This statement concerns statistical value;
it does not posit a polynomial girth oracle for a general input graph.
\end{corollary}
The retained case uses the same statistical argument on discovered error
sets, with actual matching and payment at the terminal barrier.  Its proof
is included in Appendix~\ref{app:prices}; no efficient girth oracle is
assumed for an arbitrary compatibility graph.

\begin{corollary}[A compact leading-price controller]
\label{cor:computable-price}
For laminar compatibility, the combinatorial preprocessing in
Theorem~\ref{thm:laminar} computes the depth and the critical stage
indices in~\eqref{eq:price-head} in polynomial time. It therefore returns
the exact symbolic expression for the leading coefficient in terms of
the supplied channel probabilities, as in Theorem~\ref{thm:price}; no
exact real-valued KL oracle is required. Replacing the generic subset oracle by the
capacity table implements its causal upper controller without
exponential tool-state expansion, under exactly the original resource
certificate in~\eqref{eq:price-rational-quota}--\eqref{eq:price-total-cap}.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
For the fixed initial remaining set, query the table for its initial
depth and each stage's maximum bad-child rank. Sum $A_i$ at precisely
the indices in~\eqref{eq:price-head}; this takes $O(Nqt)$
combinatorial work for $N,q\ge1$, in addition to tree construction.
During actual execution, the same table returns each required maximum
bad-child rank and a compatible attaining tool. These are the only
allocation-oracle outputs used in the risk recursion. The targets,
observations, mismatch handles, actual prices and finite caps are
unchanged. Ties in bad-child rank need not be broken by comparing real
KL expressions, because their coefficients enter only a lower-order
parent term. The rational statistical arithmetic depends on the input bit
length and numerical native quotas, as specified in the price construction;
no bound polynomial in the logarithm of the call cap is asserted.
\end{proof}

\section{Related work and the role of the structural result}
\label{sec:related}

Online matching on a known graph already has a game-theoretic formulation.
Shen~\cite{Shen06} considers a fixed bipartite graph on which an adversary
requests left vertices and a matcher must immediately choose distinct
right neighbors, without revising earlier choices.  The adversary in that
formulation may choose the request order.  Here the complete stage order
is given, and the adversary adaptively activates a subsequence of it.
Papadimitriou, Pollner, Saberi, and Wajc~\cite{PPSW21} study another close
information model: the graph and order are known, each stage arrives
independently with a known probability, and matches are irrevocable.
Their objective is expected matching reward.  Their PSPACE-hardness
construction uses general clause neighborhoods; it does not establish
hardness for laminar neighborhoods or for the minimum adversarial
activation budget causing a failure.
source_dispositions.summary: External online matching literature/complexity attribution; own input distinction only, no new proved result

source_dispositions.text:
For an arbitrary compatibility graph, our error-budget game is a finite
acyclic instance of a min-cost reachability game~\cite{BGHM15}: correct
transitions cost zero, error transitions cost one, and the allocator
chooses the compatible tool after an error.  Its Bellman recurrence and
minimax interpretation therefore use a classical framework.  An explicit
state graph, however, distinguishes remaining-tool subsets and can be
exponential in the incidence input.  The result in
Section~\ref{sec:laminar} provides a compact representation for the
specified laminar class.  If assignments can instead be retained until
the end, repairable error sets are independent sets of a transversal
matroid.  Computing the girth of such a matroid is already NP-hard; the
earlier hardness theorem and its proof are reproduced by Alexeev,
Cahill, and Mixon~\cite{ACM12}.
source_dispositions.summary: Own game/compact class/retained matroid interpretation amid external min-cost and hardness citations
source_dispositions.notes: External hardness and priority are not Lean-certified original assertions; general-graph compactness is not claimed.

source_dispositions.text:
The matroid operations underlying our representation are classical.
Fife and Oxley~\cite{FO17} study laminar matroids, their presentations,
and closure under minors.  In particular, contraction of a nonloop
decreases by one the capacity of each set containing that element.
The operation that retains precisely those independent sets extendible
by an element of a specified set $S$ is principal truncation at the flat
$\operatorname{cl}(S)$, provided that this flat has positive rank;
see Backman, Eur, and Simpson~\cite[Proposition~3.1.5 and
Lemma~3.2.4]{BES24}.  Zero rank gives our separate empty-family
symbol.  Also, the common independent sets of two capacity presentations
on the \emph{same} laminar tree are represented simply by taking the
smaller capacity at each node.  This last observation does not hold for
arbitrary intersections of matroids.
source_dispositions.summary: Same-tree capacity/VOID/intersection operations amid classical contraction/truncation attribution
source_dispositions.notes: Literature attribution and universal general-matroid contrast are context, not additional positive original theorems.

source_dispositions.text:
Our structural statement concerns the entire family of winning
used-tool sets, for every suffix and every future error budget.
All these families remain representable on the original eligibility
tree.  This invariant preserves the order of play between adaptive
activation and irrevocable allocation.  It yields polynomial
preprocessing, exact rank queries, and a causal tool-selection rule,
rather than assuming a strategy or an expanded game graph as input.
The proof is self-contained and makes the standard truncation and
intersection operations explicit.  Its statistical consequence is that
the depth and ordered coefficient in the fixed-graph leading-cost law
can be computed from the same compact representation.
source_dispositions.summary: Own ordered closure/actual strategy/compact statistical coefficient restatement

source_dispositions.text:
Generalized sequential multiple testing already studies savings from
tolerating several erroneous decisions.  Song and
Fellouris~\cite{SF19} give first-order optimality results under generalized
error metrics.  Xing's dissertation~\cite[Chapter~3]{Xing23} treats
generalized misclassification control while minimizing weighted total
sample size.  Xing and Fellouris~\cite{XF23} also give multistage signal
recovery procedures and finite-parameter calibration for tolerated
errors.  Thus total sampling cost, error tolerance, and logarithmic
testing costs are established subjects.  Our model additionally exposes
the exact truth after an irrevocable write, making the realized use of
shared reliable correction tools available to later decisions.  The
cost theorem treats that information and allocation pattern while
comparing all lawful randomized visible-history policies.  Its
asymptotic statement keeps the finite compatibility structure fixed.
source_dispositions.summary: Own post-write information/full-policy fixed-structure cost statement amid external testing survey
source_dispositions.notes: External testing results/priority not re-proved or independently verified here.

source_dispositions.text:
Feedback coding provides a precedent for multiple exponential orders
of reliability.  Mirghaderi, Goldsmith, and Weissman~\cite{MGW13}
obtain higher-order exponential error decay for the Gaussian channel
with sufficient rate-limited feedback.  Their coding and average-power
model allows a sender who knows the message to change later
transmissions.  Here the decision maker purchases observations of an
unknown state and consumes compatible one-use tools that correct
errors exactly.  We use the feedback literature as a reliability
precedent, rather than attributing exponential hierarchies themselves
to the present model.

Combinatorial selection with costly information~\cite{Chawla24} models
information acquisition by local Markov decision processes and proves
generalized composition guarantees, not only matroid-specific ones.
It also shows that inappropriate local approximations can produce large
global losses.  We do not claim a new general composition principle.
Finally, the extended Littlestone
dimension~\cite{ZC16} characterizes a minimax tradeoff between mistakes
and abstentions.  This supplies a relevant precedent for game-based
error parameters; its version-space state, prediction actions, and
mistake/abstention objective differ from the fixed-order allocation game
and paid statistical cost considered here.
source_dispositions.summary: External feedback/costly-information/Littlestone precedents and distinctions; no new theorem of this paper

A capacity vector is \emph{normalized} if its singleton capacities lie
in $\{0,1\}$, all capacities are nonnegative, and every internal node
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 c_T\le\sum_{C\text{ a child of }T}c_C.
 \label{eq:laminar-normalized}
\end{equation}
Starting from capacities $0\le c_T\le |T|$, normalize by processing
nodes from leaves to top and replacing each internal capacity by
\[
 c_T\leftarrow
 \min\left\{c_T,\sum_{C\text{ a child of }T}c_C\right\}.
\]
This does not change $\mathcal I(c)$: the children partition $T$, so
their constraints already imply the additional upper bound.  The
operation costs $O(t)$ and leaves every capacity in $[0,q]$.

\begin{lemma}[Extension by one compatible tool]
\label{lem:laminar-extension}
Let $c$ be normalized, let $D\in\mathcal I(c)$, and let
$\varnothing\ne S\in\mathcal L$.  There exists
$r\in S\setminus D$ such that $D\cup\{r\}\in\mathcal I(c)$ if and
only if
\begin{equation}
 |D\cap T|<c_T\qquad\text{for every }T\in\mathcal A(S).
 \label{eq:laminar-strict-path}
\end{equation}
When it exists, such a tool can be found by a descent in the tree.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Adding a tool in $S$ increases the count at every node of
$\mathcal A(S)$, which proves necessity.  For sufficiency, call a node
$T$ \emph{slack} when $|D\cap T|<c_T$.  If an internal node $T$ is
slack, then
\[
 \sum_{C\text{ a child of }T}|D\cap C|
 =|D\cap T|
 <c_T
 \le\sum_{C\text{ a child of }T}c_C.
\]
Thus at least one child is slack.  Start at $S$, which is slack by
\eqref{eq:laminar-strict-path}, and repeatedly choose a slack child.
At the resulting singleton $\{r\}$, slackness and integrality give
$|D\cap\{r\}|=0$ and $c_{\{r\}}=1$, so $r$ is unused.  Every node
containing $r$ is either on the selected descent or an ancestor of
$S$.  All these nodes are slack, and all other counts remain unchanged.
Consequently $D\cup\{r\}$ satisfies every capacity constraint.
The descent examines at most $O(t)$ nodes and child entries.
\end{proof}
source_dispositions.summary: Full extension lemma, slack-child proof and local probes
Original one-tool extension family

source_dispositions.text:
\begin{lemma}[Closure on one tree]
\label{lem:laminar-closure}
The following operations preserve normalized capacity representations,
with $\mathsf{VOID}$ allowed, and cost $O(t)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For normalized $c$ and nonempty $S\in\mathcal L$, the family
$\mathcal E_S(\mathcal I(c))$ is obtained by decreasing $c_T$ by one
for every $T\in\mathcal A(S)$.  If any of these capacities was zero,
the result is $\mathsf{VOID}$; otherwise the resulting vector is already
normalized.
\item The intersection of two capacity families is represented by the
coordinatewise minimum of their vectors, followed by normalization.
\end{enumerate}
Also $\mathcal E_\varnothing(\mathcal I)=\mathsf{VOID}$,
$\mathcal E_S(\mathsf{VOID})=\mathsf{VOID}$, and an intersection with
$\mathsf{VOID}$ is $\mathsf{VOID}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If $D\cup\{r\}\in\mathcal I(c)$, then $D\in\mathcal I(c)$ by
downward closure.  Lemma~\ref{lem:laminar-extension} therefore
characterizes the extension family by the original inequalities and
strict inequalities on $\mathcal A(S)$.  For integer counts, these are
exactly the asserted decremented capacities.  If a path capacity was
zero, its strict inequality is impossible.  Otherwise capacities stay
nonnegative.  At an internal node $S$ only the left side of
\eqref{eq:laminar-normalized} decreases.  At a strict ancestor of $S$,
its own capacity and exactly one child's capacity both decrease by one.
Thus normalization is preserved.  Finally,
$\mathcal I(c)\cap\mathcal I(c')=\mathcal I(\min(c,c'))$ directly
from the defining inequalities, and normalization does not change
this family.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Implementation and boundaries}

For completeness, an explicit incidence representation suffices for
the preprocessing claimed in Theorem~\ref{thm:laminar}.  Add $U$ and
the singleton sets, delete duplicate sets, and compare all pairs for
containment or disjointness.  For each non-top node, select its
smallest proper superset as its parent.  Laminarity makes this parent
unique.  The singleton additions ensure that children cover their
parent.  There are at most $N+q+1$ nodes, so direct membership scans
give the stated $O((N+q+1)^2q)$ bound.  This claim concerns explicit
sets; it assumes no succinct-set oracle.

\begin{proof}
A posterior-error SPRT with target $p$ has Bayes error at most $p$.
The log-likelihood increments are bounded and have true-direction drift
$D_{ix}>0$.  Bounded overshoot and stopped drift give
\[
 \E_x[c_iT]\le \frac{c_i}{D_{ix}}
             \bigl(\log(1/p)+O_i(1)\bigr).
\]
Integrability follows, for example, by a bounded-increment tail bound for
the positive-drift score before applying stopped drift.  Setting $p=1/t$
gives the asserted upper asymptotic.  A zero-observation guess gives
$J_i(t)\le t$, and these two constructions give the global logarithmic bound.

For the lower bound it suffices to consider tests with objective at most
$2A_i\log t$; more expensive tests already exceed the desired bound.
Their Bayes error is $O_i(\log t/t)$.  Positivity of both fixed prior masses
implies the same bound for each conditional error
$\alpha=\Prob_0(\widehat X=1)$ and
$\beta=\Prob_1(\widehat X=0)$.  Stopped relative entropy and data processing
for the final decision give
\[
 D_{i0}\E_0T\ge\operatorname{kl}(1-\alpha,\beta),\qquad
 D_{i1}\E_1T\ge\operatorname{kl}(1-\beta,\alpha).
\]
For finite expected sample sizes these follow by summing the predictable
log-likelihood increments; the infinite-expectation case needs no bound.
Using
$\operatorname{kl}(1-u,v)\ge(1-u)\log(1/v)-\log2$ and averaging with
the original prior yields
\[
 c_i\E T\ge A_i\bigl(\log t-\log\log t-O_i(1)\bigr).
\]
The argument applies to the actual decision, so it does not impose MAP.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Full-history penalty bridge]\label{lem:price-bridge}
From every healthy native history at the first entry to stage $i$, with unused tools $R$, every legal policy satisfies
\[
 \E[\text{future actual observation charges}]
 +\lambda\Prob(\text{eventual task failure})\ge G_{i,R}(\lambda).
\]
This includes policies that delay an already allocated correction, abandon
before a write, or continue to incur charges after permanent failure.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Induct on the number of remaining stages.  Condition on all already
generated history and the private random seed.  Native freshness preserves
the current prior and conditional i.i.d. channel; it does not merely
preserve an average error rate.  The observations before the ordinary write
and its actual binary output form a legal sequential experiment.  The
correct continuation costs at least $G_g$.  After an erroneous write every
actual compatible allocation costs at least $G_b$; refusing a required
allocation or any permanent failure costs $\lambda\ge G_b$.
Thus their combined lower bound is
$G_g+\E[c_iT+(G_b-G_g)\ind\{\widehat X\ne X_i\}]$.

If the policy abandons before its ordinary write, retain every observation
it already bought and fill in an arbitrary binary decision for analysis.
The virtual continuation assigned to either outcome is at most $\lambda$,
so this replacement cannot increase the original comparison charge.
It does not declare abandonment successful or reveal a future fact to the
implemented policy.  Spending after permanent failure is nonnegative and
can be discarded.  These observations give the lower half of
\eqref{eq:price-penalty}, including immediate abandonment.  Conversely,
near-optimal local tests and near-optimal continuations implement its
right side to arbitrary accuracy, proving the recursion itself.

If allocated corrections may legally execute later, freely complete those
obligations only in the lower-bound relaxation.  Their tools remain
occupied.  Simulate the original history and its execution ledger; this
provides no new information and does not force earlier real payment.
Only one failure penalty is charged throughout this induction.
\end{proof}
source_dispositions.summary: Authorized first-entry full-history bridge and near-optimal continuation construction

\subsection{Penalty asymptotics, including cancellation at equal ranks}

\begin{lemma}[Rank and leading penalty coefficient]\label{lem:price-penalty-asymptotic}
At a fixed healthy state, $\rho=\infty$ implies $G=0$.  If
$\rho(i,R)=d<\infty$, then
\begin{equation}
 G_{i,R}(\lambda)=C(i,R)\ell_d(\lambda)(1+o(1)),\qquad C(i,R)>0.
 \label{eq:price-penalty-asymptotic}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Infinite rank means every error pattern has a causal repair strategy, so
blind writes and free relaxed corrections have value zero.  For finite
rank use backward induction.  Among finitely many bad successors the
smallest penalty value first selects the largest rank, and among equal
ranks selects the smallest leading coefficient.  Hence, when
$1\le d_b<\infty$, $G_b$ has a positive multiple of
$\ell_{d_b}(\lambda)$ as its leading term.

The case $d_g=d_b<\infty$ requires care: leading terms of $G_b-G_g$
may cancel.  No lower bound on that difference is needed.  Instead,
\[
 0\le J_i(G_b-G_g)\le O_i\bigl(\log(1+G_b)\bigr)
      =o(\ell_{d_g}(\lambda)).
\]
The correct continuation therefore supplies the entire leading term,
as prescribed by \eqref{eq:price-coefficient}.

If $d_g>d_b\ge1$, then $G_g=o(G_b)$, including the case $d_g=\infty$.
Consequently $G_b-G_g\sim G_b$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:price-local} gives
\[
 J_i(G_b-G_g)\sim A_i\ell_{d_b+1}(\lambda).
\]
If $d_b=0$, then $G_b=\lambda$, while $G_g=o(\lambda)$, so the same
statement holds with $\ell_1$.  Comparing this term with the correct
continuation retains the smaller depth, and adds their coefficients when
the depths agree.  This is exactly \eqref{eq:price-coefficient}.  The
minimum with $\lambda$ is eventually inactive.  Induction also proves
positivity of every finite-rank coefficient.
\end{proof}
source_dispositions.summary: Strict shorter-suffix asymptotics, tied child minimum and equal-rank cancellation

source_dispositions.text:
For a $\delta$-safe native policy take $\lambda=1/\delta$ in the bridge.
Its actual variable cost is at least
$G_{1,U}(1/\delta)-1$, proving the lower bound in
Theorem~\ref{thm:price} for the full comparator.
For \eqref{eq:price-head}, along the all-correct path $R$ stays fixed and
$\rho(i,R)$ is nondecreasing.  The equality $b_i=d-1$ forces
$\rho(i,R)=d$, while after the correct-path rank exceeds $d$ no further
term contributes at depth $d$.  Expanding \eqref{eq:price-coefficient}
along this path proves the formula.

\subsection{A matching causal controller}

First define an untruncated reference controller.  Its state has a rational
risk parameter $0<r\le1/4$, initially $r=\delta/2$.  Define, by integer
comparisons,
\[
 B_1(r)=\lceil\log_2(1/r)\rceil,\qquad
 B_{j+1}(r)=\lceil\log_2(2+B_j(r))\rceil,\qquad
 p_j(r)=\frac1{4(1+B_j(r))}.
\]
For each fixed $j\ge1$,
\begin{equation}
 \log(1/p_j(r))=\ell_{j+1}(1/r)+O_j(1),\qquad
 p_j(r)=O_j(1/\ell_j(1/r)).
 \label{eq:price-threshold-asymptotic}
\end{equation}
At a healthy state apply the following rule.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
\item If $\rho=\infty$, take no observations, write blindly, and after each
actual reported error choose an infinite-rank child and execute its real
compatible correction.
\item If $d_b=0$, use a posterior-error SPRT of target $p=r/2$ and write
MAP.  After a correct report continue with risk $r/2$; after an error the
task fails and the controller may abandon.
\item Otherwise $d_b\ge1$ is finite.  Use target $p=p_{d_b}(r)$ and write
MAP.  After a correct report continue with risk $r/2$.  After an error
execute a real correction using any tool maximizing the bad-child rank,
and continue with
\[
 r'=\min\{1/4,r/(2p)\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
There is no missing finite-rank case with $d_b=\infty$, since
$d_g\ge d_b$ would make the current rank infinite.  The laminar table
supplies exactly the ranks and tools required by this rule; the rule does
not require comparison of real-valued coefficients between equal-rank
children.
source_dispositions.summary: Original rational thresholds and actual three-branch causal controller

source_dispositions.text:
At every entry history the local error probability $e$ is at most $p$.
In the third case the correct branch contributes risk at most $r/2$ and
the error branch at most $pr'\le r/2$.  The second case has the same bound,
and the first has zero failure risk.  Induction therefore bounds reference
risk by $r$.  These local allocations are a construction of an upper
bound, not extra constraints on the comparator.

For the cost induction, $r'\ge r$ and $r'\to0$ as $r\to0$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:price-local}'s SPRT construction gives local expected cost
\[
 A_i\log(1/p)+O_i(1)
 =A_i\ell_{d_b+1}(1/r)+O_i(1)
\]
in the third case.  The error child's observation cost is
$O(\ell_{d_b}(1/r'))=O(\ell_{d_b}(1/r))$; multiplying by
$e\le p=O(1/\ell_{d_b}(1/r))$ leaves only $O(1)$.
The correct child's leading term is unchanged by $r\mapsto r/2$.
The case $d_b=0$ gives $A_i\log(1/r)+O_i(1)$.  Comparing the terms
therefore gives exactly \eqref{eq:price-coefficient} as an upper bound.
Every actual correction, including one on a later-failing path, is charged.
Their pathwise total is at most $\min(N,q)f_{\max}$, which is $O(1)$ and
does not affect any finite-depth divergent leading term.

\subsection{A rational certificate for the original native caps}
\label{subsec:price-native}

No controller receives an enlarged observation window or a new tool.  Along
any reference path, $r\ge\delta/2^{N+1}$.  For $r\le1/4$,
$B_j(r)\le B_1(r)\le1/r$, hence $p_j(r)\ge r/6$; the no-tool target
$r/2$ has the same bound.  Put
\[
 C_N=6\cdot2^{N+1},\qquad b_{\max}=\log(C_N/\delta),
\]
so every tested posterior target is at least $\delta/C_N$.

For the fixed channel let
\[
 d_i=\min_xD_{ix},\quad
 M_i=\max_y\left|\log\frac{P_i^1(y)}{P_i^0(y)}\right|,\quad
 L_i=\left|\log\frac{\pi_i(1)}{\pi_i(0)}\right|.
\]
An analytic sufficient observation quota is
\begin{equation}
 Q_i=\left\lceil\max\left\{
 \frac{2(b_{\max}+L_i)}{d_i},\quad
 \frac{8M_i^2}{d_i^2}\log\frac{2N}{\delta}
 \right\}\right\rceil.
 \label{eq:price-analytic-quota}
\end{equation}
Indeed, conditional on any entry history and true state, failure of the
ideal SPRT to stop by $Q_i$ implies its true-direction score is below
$b_{\max}+L_i$.  Its mean is at least $d_iQ_i$, and its increment range
has length at most $2M_i$.  Hoeffding's bound and
\eqref{eq:price-analytic-quota} yield overflow probability at most
$\delta/(2N)$.

The native stage windows and quotas must permit these actual
$\widehat Q_i$ observations and the ordinary write, report, and lawful
correction operations.  If $H_0$ counts the other required calls in a full
run, require the original total call cap to satisfy
\begin{equation}
 H\ge H_0+\sum_{i=1}^N\widehat Q_i+\min(N,q).
 \label{eq:price-total-cap}
\end{equation}
If a test exhausts $\widehat Q_i$ without stopping, abandon the entire task.
A union bound adds at most $\delta/2$ overflow risk to the reference risk
$\delta/2$.  Couple the actual and reference policies on the same
observation tapes: until the first overflow they coincide, and then the
actual policy stops and deletes only future nonnegative charges.  Its
pathwise cost is thus at most the reference cost, including every correction
already executed on a path that ultimately fails.  This proves the upper
bound in Theorem~\ref{thm:price} under the stated native certificate.

the numerical call quotas, and is not claimed polynomial in $\log H$.

\begin{remark}[Normal charges]\label{rem:price-normal-charges}
If a completed run incurs an additional fixed normal charge $C_0$, any
$\delta$-safe policy pays it on an event of probability at least $1-\delta$.
Thus its total-cost lower bound adds $(1-\delta)C_0$, and the constructed
upper bound adds at most $C_0$.  These are real charges, as are all fixed
correction prices.  Neither changes the divergent leading terms.
\end{remark}

an error adds i, or fails if $H\cup\{i\}$ is dependent.  There is no

additional errors causing dependence is exactly
\[
 d_R(i,H)=\min\{|E|:E\subseteq\{i,\ldots,N\},\ H\cup E
                       \text{ is dependent}\}.
\]

experiment, single-penalty bridge, equal-rank cancellation, and risk

Initially the smallest dependent set has size g, because every dependent
set contains a circuit.  Along the all-correct path H is empty.  Its bad
successor has rank $g-1$ exactly when there is a dependent set of size g
whose first index is i.  Every size-g dependent set is itself a circuit,
by minimality of g.  Conversely any size-g circuit with first index i gives
such a bad continuation.  Formula~\eqref{eq:price-head}, now for these

\section{Proof of the star separation and its own cap certificate}
\label{app:star}
Use the star and the three contracts of Proposition~\ref{prop:star}, with
$n=q+1$.  This appendix proves matching upper bounds with a separate
common certificate.  It invokes only the cap-independent lower bounds
of the general price laws, not an unproved comparison of quota formulas.
\subsection{Matching and the two early-report prices}

An error set E in \eqref{eq:example-star} is matchable if and only if
$|E|\le q$.  If stage 1 is correct, match every erroneous singleton to its
own tool.  If stage 1 is erroneous but $|E|\le q$, some singleton j is
correct; assign tool j to stage 1 and every erroneous singleton its own
tool.  All $q+1$ errors exceed capacity and cannot be matched.  Thus the
only circuit is the set of all stages, so ER has g=q+1 and a single
minimum-circuit head, 1.  The cap-independent lower-bound part of
Corollary~\ref{thm:retained} gives the ER price lower bound.  The explicit
controllers below attain it under this section's common certificate.

For I, one error is always repairable.  After an error at stage 1, whichever
tool j the policy actually consumes, the adaptive adversary can next cause
an error at singleton j.  Hence $\rho=2$.  The only critical index in
\eqref{eq:price-head} is stage 1: if it is correct, all remaining stages
can simultaneously be repaired.  Thus C=a and the cap-independent
lower-bound part of Theorem~\ref{thm:price} gives the I lower bound;
the explicit controller below supplies its matching upper bound.
This argument allows the adversary to see the realized
tool; it does not replace it by a fixed two-error sequence.

In the order with singletons first, repair each erroneous singleton by its
own tool, and repair an erroneous final universal stage by any unused tool.
This succeeds for every pattern of at most q errors.  All $q+1$ errors
fail, so $\rho=g=q+1$.  Only the first singleton can head the unique
size-$q+1$ obstruction, and the coefficient remains a.  Reordering the
stages changes online price even though every compatibility-set count and
every offline matchability relation is unchanged.
source_dispositions.summary: Original two-order star, matchability/girth/independent causal rank and coefficients

source_dispositions.text:
\subsection{The late-report lower bound}

We give a separate proof because the early-report history recursion does
not apply before late reports.  For a fair BSC fact let p be its posterior
MAP error at stopping and define
\[
 \phi(p)=(1-2p)\log\frac{1-p}{p},\qquad 0<p\le1/2.
\]
Each true-direction log-likelihood increment has expectation $\kappa$.
Conditional on the stopped transcript, the stopped cumulative
true-direction score has expectation $\phi(p)$.
Bounded-increment stopped Wald, or direct stopped summation under a finite
native quota, therefore gives
\begin{equation}
 c\E T=a\E\phi(p),\qquad
 \log(1/p)-2\le\phi(p)\le\log(1/p).
 \label{eq:example-bsc-information}
\end{equation}
The first inequality follows by bounding
$2p\log(1/p)-(1-2p)\log(1-p)\le2$.
source_dispositions.summary: Actual stopped posterior information/phi and local BSC cost

source_dispositions.text:
Let Z be the complete transcript before the first true report, including
private random seeds and any abandonment; unvisited facts retain their
fair priors.  Conditional on Z the hidden bits have a product posterior.
Indeed, after fixing the seed and transcript, the sampling, stopping, and
writing rules contribute common factors, and the remaining likelihood is
the product of the separate BSC likelihoods.  This remains true when the
numbers of observations depend on earlier visible history.  Let $p_i(Z)$
be the individual MAP errors, with $p_i=1/2$ for an unvisited stage, and let
$s(Z)$ be the conditional ultimate failure probability of the original
policy.  An abandoned transcript has s=1.  Otherwise its fixed ordinary
writes have independent conditional errors, each at least $p_i(Z)$.
The all-error set is unmatchable, even if the policy later makes the best
possible repairs.  Consequently
\[
 s(Z)\ge\prod_{i=1}^n p_i(Z).
\]
Apply \eqref{eq:example-bsc-information} to each actual stopped experiment
and sum \emph{before} conditioning on any success-selected event.  Jensen's
inequality now yields, for every $\delta$-safe LR policy,
\begin{align*}
 \E C_{\mathrm{obs}}
 &=a\E\sum_i\phi(p_i(Z))\\
 &\ge a\E\sum_i\log(1/p_i(Z))-2an\\
 &\ge a\E\log(1/s(Z))-2an\\
 &\ge a\log(1/\delta)-2an.
\end{align*}
Infinite expected cost already satisfies the bound.  It covers non-MAP
writes, random stopping, abandonment, arbitrary final repair decisions,
and spending on failed paths.  It also applies when the universal stage
is last, since the same all-error event is the unique matching obstruction.
source_dispositions.summary: Actual pre-report record and non-MAP/failure/universe lower

source_dispositions.text:
\subsection{Explicit controllers and one common finite certificate}

For completeness the following controllers achieve the three coefficients
under one common quota.  Write $r_0=\delta/2\le1/4$ and use the rational
functions $p_j(r)$ from Section~\ref{sec:prices}.  A BSC posterior-error
SPRT of target p satisfies
\[
 \E C_{\mathrm{obs}}\le a[\log(1/p)+h].
\]

For I on the universal-first order, test stage 1 to target $p_1(r_0)$.
After a correct report, blindly write each singleton and actually repair
its errors with its own tool.  After an erroneous first write, consume
tool 1 and pay for that correction; only singleton 1 has lost its tool.
Test that singleton to target
$r'=\min\{1/4,r_0/p_1(r_0)\}$, and blind-write and repair the others.
Risk is at most $p_1(r_0)r'\le r_0$, and total expected observation cost is
\[
 a[\log(1/p_1(r_0))+h]
 +p_1(r_0)a[\log(1/r')+h]
 =a\ell_2(1/\delta)+O(1).
\]
The already executed first correction is charged even if singleton 1 later
fails.
source_dispositions.summary: Original UF current script plus actual risk/cost and additive real-delta normalization

source_dispositions.text:
For ER maintain only the count of actual uncorrected error obligations,
without making an early tool commitment.  While all previous tested writes
have been erroneous and there remain $k+1$ stages and k effective tools,
test the next stage to target $p_k(r)$ if $k\ge1$, and to target r if k=0.
A correct report makes all remaining stages safe to blind-write: the final
error count is then at most q.  An erroneous report changes k to $k-1$ and
$r$ to $\min\{1/4,r/p_k(r)\}$.  At the barrier execute the explicit real
matching above when it exists, and otherwise abandon.  Induction gives
risk at most r and expected observation costs
\[
 F_0(r)\le a[\log(1/r)+h],\qquad
 F_k(r)\le a[\log(1/p_k(r))+h]+p_k(r)F_{k-1}(r'),
\]
whence $F_k(r)\le a\ell_{k+1}(1/r)(1+o(1))$ by
\eqref{eq:price-threshold-asymptotic}.  The error branch contributes only
O(1).  On the singleton-first order the same count controller is also
legal for I: immediately execute each erroneous singleton's correction
with its own tool, and correct an erroneous final universal stage with
any still-unused tool.  The universal stage is last.  Thus the same
observation recursion supplies the matching upper bound even when
physical correction must be completed inside its current window.
source_dispositions.summary: Real count-budget early scripts, true retained terminal matching/current payment

source_dispositions.text:
For LR, test just the first fact to posterior target $\delta/2$ and
blind-write the others.  After all reports arrive, perform the real
matching unless all writes were erroneous.  Failure is contained in the
first tested error, so risk is at most $\delta/2$, with observation cost
$a\log(1/\delta)+O(1)$.
Every one of these policies makes at most q actual corrections and pays
their full pathwise bill, at most qf.  Retained-port controllers never
interpret their virtual obligation count as an already executed free
correction.
source_dispositions.summary: Actual first-stage-only late script and true terminal law

source_dispositions.text:
All of these reference controllers have tested targets at least
$\delta/10$: their visited r never falls below $\delta/2$, and
$p_k(r)\ge r/[4(1+r)]\ge r/5$.  Define the rationally computable integers
\begin{equation}
 E_* =\min\{e\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:2^e\ge20n/\delta\},\qquad
 Q_* =\left\lceil\frac{2E_*}{\gamma^2}\right\rceil.
 \label{eq:example-common-quota}
\end{equation}
Require each original observation window and quota to allow $Q_*$ samples
and its lawful write, report, and correction operations, and require
\[
 H\ge H_0+nQ_*+q.
\]
For either truth the true-direction score has increment range length 2h
and mean $\kappa\ge8\gamma^2$.  Its required log-odds boundary is at most
$\log(10/\delta)\le E_*$.  Since
$Q_*\ge2E_*/\kappa$, Hoeffding gives
\[
 \Prob(T_{\mathrm{ideal}}>Q_*\mid\text{entry history},X)
 \le\exp\!\left(-\frac{\kappa^2Q_*}{8h^2}\right)
 =e^{-\gamma^2Q_*/2}\le e^{-E_*}\le\frac{\delta}{2n}.
\]
Abandon the entire task on any quota overflow.  At most n tests give total
overflow risk at most $\delta/2$, so native risk is at most $\delta$.

The same-tape coupling deletes only future nonnegative charges at an
overflow and retains all earlier paid observations and corrections.
Posterior odds are rational powers of $(1+2\gamma)/(1-2\gamma)$ compared
with rational thresholds; no exact logarithm or KL oracle is required.

\section{Independent extension: correction prices in a shared pool}
\label{sec:paid-extension}
\paragraph{Logical status and independence.}
This appendix records an independent, restricted extension. It is not
part of the main theorem collection. The structural theorem, the
fixed-structure statistical theorem, the star separation and their
proofs in Appendices~\ref{app:laminar}, \ref{app:prices} and
\ref{app:star} do not invoke any result in this appendix.
Its stricter homogeneous shared-pool and current-payment assumptions
are not assumptions of the main results. The corollary below uses
the main statistical theorem in one direction only; there is no
dependence from the main proof chain back to this extension.
source_dispositions.summary: Independent appendix status and one-way main-to-Paid dependency; checked by receipt/import graph

source_dispositions.text:
The structural law above fixes correction fees while confidence increases.
This section isolates the effect of a fee that may vary with the other
parameters.  It is a restricted extension: all $K<N$ tools can correct
every output, facts are independent fair bits, and every review is a
homogeneous BSC of accuracy $1/2+\gamma$ costing $c$.
Assume rational $c>0$, $0<\gamma\le1/4$, $f\ge0$ and
$0<\delta\le1/64$.  Each actual correction costs the same $f$.
The hypotheses concerning freshness, genuine mismatch handles, exact
early reports, guaranteed one-use corrections and all-path charging
remain as in Section~\ref{sec:model}.

We strengthen the current-allocation contract to \emph{current payment},
denoted $I_{\rm pay}$: a wrong output must be physically corrected and
paid for before advance.  An irrevocable allocation with execution or
payment withheld until a later decision is not this contract.
All lawful randomized visible-history policies remain in the comparison,
including non-MAP writes, abandonment and spending on eventual failures.
Original review quotas and the total call cap remain in force; there is
no additional hard monetary spending cap.

Let $R_{\rm act}$ count physically executed corrections.  Define
$V_f^{\rm nat}(\delta)$ as the infimum of
\begin{equation}
 \E C=\E\!\left[c\sum_{i=1}^N T_i+fR_{\rm act}\right]
 \quad\text{subject to }\Prob(\mathrm{failure})\le\delta
 \label{eq:paid:bill}
\end{equation}
in this original instance.  Let $V_f^\infty(\delta)$ relax only review
and call caps, retaining the same correction rights and payment contract.
Write $h=\log((1+2\gamma)/(1-2\gamma))$ and $a=c/(2\gamma h)$ as before.
Appendix~\ref{app:paid:proofs} gives an explicit integer
$Q=Q(N,\gamma,\delta)$, independent of $f$, in
\eqref{eq:paid:certificate-numbers}.  The sufficient native qualification is
\begin{equation}
 \text{each original stage admits $Q$ reviews and its lawful operations},
 \qquad H\ge H_0+NQ+K.
 \label{eq:paid:cap-certificate}
\end{equation}
It is a test of the original resources, not permission to enlarge them.
It is separate from the fixed-structure certificate
in Appendix~\ref{subsec:price-native}.
source_dispositions.summary: Original shared pool/BSC/actual Ipay, values and fee-independent original numerical qualification
Full same-native separation and actual eight-factor algorithm/time

source_dispositions.text:
The price is therefore controlled by a free baseline, an additional
$aN\log(1+f/a)$ scale, and saturation at the cost of avoiding corrections.
This does not determine $A$ uniformly in $N,K,\delta$, and is not a fee
law for arbitrary laminar compatibility.

Three mechanisms underlie the theorem.  First, an uncapped simulation of
any free full-history policy improves its local experiments so that
actual errors form a subset of its virtual errors.  Only genuine errors
are corrected and paid for; the task risk does not increase.
Second, stopping at the first permanent failure charges every preceding
actual correction, while only one failure allowance is needed.  With
$r=\E R_{\rm act}$ and $m=N(1-\delta)$ this yields
\[
 \E C\ge a m\phi\!\left(\min\{1/2,(r+\delta)/m\}\right)+fr,
 \qquad \phi(p)=(1-2p)\log\frac{1-p}{p}.
\]
Third, a rational penalty program and a mixture of two policies attain
the original risk; deeper capped tests mixed with blind guesses preserve
each local error \emph{exactly}.  This supplies the necessary native
implementation, rather than executing an unbounded simulator under a
hard quota.  Appendix~\ref{app:paid:proofs} contains the complete chain,
including the eight-factor algorithm.
source_dispositions.summary: Mechanisms/parameter scope and actual calibrated native implementation

\paragraph{Relation to established testing tools.}
Sequential Bayes testing and constrained-test optimization are also
established.  Fau\ss{} and Zoubir~\cite{FZ15} develop a linear-programming
approach; their continuous likelihood-ratio assumption is not a direct
proof of the finite-BSC randomized boundary calculation used here.
Vershinin, Cohen, and Gurewitz~\cite{VCG26} study cost-aware acquisition
and its asymptotic optimality, so optimizing actual acquisition cost is
not itself a novelty claim.  Li, Li, Wang, and Liu~\cite{LLWL16} impose
online expected sensor-usage constraints in finite-horizon testing;
our original call limit is pathwise.  The local tests, penalty methods
and initial policy mixing remain classical tools.  The extension's
specific content is the risk-preserving full-history simulation, the
actual-usage lower bound and their same-risk bounded implementation,
which together imply the displayed price reduction.

\begin{corollary}[Fixed shared pool with a growing correction price]
\label{cor:fixed-pool-price}
Fix integers $N\ge1$, $0\le K<N$ and rational $c>0$,
$0<\gamma\le1/4$.  In the shared-pool $I_{\rm pay}$ model, consider
original contracts satisfying \eqref{eq:joint-certificate} as
$\delta\downarrow0$.  For any nonnegative rational price
$f=f(\delta)$, put
\[
 B_\delta=a(N-K)\ell_{K+1}(1/\delta),\qquad
 T_B=\min\{B_\delta+aN\log(1+f/a),\ aN\log(1+N/\delta)\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \frac{1-o(1)}{129}\,T_B
 \ \le\ V_f^{\rm nat}(\delta)\ \le\ 72(1+o(1))\,T_B.
\]
The $o(1)$ is independent of $f$ and of the choice of qualified native
caps, but may depend on the fixed $N,K,c,\gamma$.  In particular
$V_f^{\rm nat}(\delta)\asymp T_B$.  This is a small-risk statement for
a fixed pool, not an all-parameter uniform frontier or a sharp leading
coefficient for growing $f$.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{Complete proofs of the independent extension}
\label{app:paid:proofs}
All results in this appendix use the fair homogeneous BSC shared-pool
model and the stricter $I_{\rm pay}$ contract of
Section~\ref{sec:paid-extension}.  Native and cap-relaxed values retain
this same contract.  In particular, relaxing a review quota does not
create a retained correction right or a free physical overwrite.

\subsubsection{Explicit native resource certificate}
Let
\[
 R=\frac{1+2\gamma}{1-2\gamma},\quad h=\log R,\quad
 \kappa=2\gamma h,\quad a=c/\kappa.
\]
All logarithms are natural unless a base is displayed.  Define
\begin{align}
 t_0&=\min\{t\ge1:t\text{ odd},\ (1-4\gamma^2)^t
                              \le(\delta/(2N))^2\},\nonumber\\
 B&=cNt_0,\qquad \Lambda=4B/\delta,\qquad
 \varepsilon=c/(3\Lambda),\nonumber\\
 p_m&=(1+R^m)^{-1},\qquad
 M=\min\{m\ge0:p_m\le c/\Lambda\},\nonumber\\
 E&=\min\{e\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:2^{-e}\le\gamma\varepsilon\},\nonumber\\
 Q&=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{M+1}{\gamma}\right\rceil,
                    \left\lceil\frac{2E}{\gamma^2}\right\rceil\right\}.
 \label{eq:paid:certificate-numbers}
\end{align}
The numbers $M,\varepsilon,Q$ depend only on $N,\gamma,\delta$,
because $c/\Lambda=\delta/(4Nt_0)$.
All comparisons in this definition are rational and computable without
approximating a logarithm.  Qualification is exactly
\eqref{eq:paid:cap-certificate}; the certificates from other theorems
are neither substituted for it nor implied by it without proof.
