\subsubsection{The exact local experiment and history representation}
\label{sec:paid:local}

Set
\[
 \phi(p)=(1-2p)\log\frac{1-p}{p},\qquad 0<p\le1/2.
\]
It is decreasing and convex, with
$\phi''(p)=1/[p^2(1-p)^2]$.  For a stopped fair-BSC experiment let $P$
be its posterior MAP error, before any truth report.

\begin{lemma}[Stopped information]
\label{lem:paid:information}
For every experiment with finite expected review count,
\begin{equation}
 c\E T=a\E\phi(P).
 \label{eq:paid:information}
\end{equation}
The identity also holds after restriction to an event determined before
the current fresh fact is born.  A fact filled blindly for analysis has
$T=0$ and $P=1/2$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Orient each log-likelihood increment by the true bit.  Its conditional
mean before purchase is $\kappa$ and its absolute value is $h$.
Summing predictable increments gives expected stopped score
$\kappa\E T$; finite expected $T$ justifies the interchange since the
increments are bounded.  Conditional on the stopped transcript, if the
posterior of bit one is $\theta$, the expected oriented score is
$(2\theta-1)\log(\theta/(1-\theta))=\phi(P)$.
This proves the identity.  Conditional on generated pre-birth history,
freshness preserves the fair prior and original channel.  Apply the same
argument there and average the indicated pre-birth event.  No step
conditions on eventual success.
\end{proof}
source_dispositions.summary: Actual gated stopped posterior information and no success conditioning

source_dispositions.text:
For $m\ge0$, define
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf C_m=\frac{cm}{2\gamma}(1-2p_m)
     =a\,mh\tanh(mh/2),\qquad (p_0,\mathsf C_0)=(1/2,0).
 \label{eq:paid:roc-points}
\end{equation}
The notation $\mathsf C_m$ denotes local review charges, distinct from the normal full-run charge $C_0$.
Let $g(p)$ be the piecewise-linear interpolation of the adjacent points
$(p_m,\mathsf C_m)$, and set $g(0)=+\infty$.

\begin{lemma}[Exact randomized local ROC]
\label{lem:paid:roc}
The minimum expected review charge of a MAP experiment with average error
exactly $p\in(0,1/2]$ is $g(p)$.  The minimum for an arbitrary binary
decision of error $e\in(0,1)$ is
$\widetilde g(e)=g(\min\{e,1-e\})$.
Each $g(p)$ is attained by randomizing two adjacent symmetric likelihood
boundary tests.  For rational $p,c,\gamma$, their probabilities and mean
charges are rational and explicitly computable.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
After any stopped record, including its private seed, posterior odds are
$R^s$ for an integer signed observation sum $s$.  Thus $P=p_m$ for some
$m=|s|$.  By Lemma~\ref{lem:paid:information}, the error/cost pair is a convex
combination of $(p_m,a\phi(p_m))=(p_m,\mathsf C_m)$.
Strict convexity of $\phi$ makes their adjacent chords the lower convex
boundary.  Consequently a MAP experiment of mean error $p$ costs at
least $g(p)$.

The symmetric random walk stopped at $\pm m$ has posterior error exactly
$p_m$.  Its finite absorbing walk has finite mean duration, and stopped
drift gives
\[
 \E T_m=\frac{m}{2\gamma}(1-2p_m).
\]
It therefore attains $\mathsf C_m$.  Mixing adjacent boundaries attains each
chord.  For any decision and its complement, both conditional error
probabilities are at least the posterior MAP error.  Hence
$\min(e,1-e)\ge\E P$.  Convexity and monotonicity yield
$\E C\ge g(\E P)\ge\widetilde g(e)$.  Complementing the symmetric
decision when $e>1/2$ attains this bound.  Finally $R^m,p_m,\mathsf C_m$ and
adjacent interpolation weights are rational for rational inputs.
\end{proof}
source_dispositions.summary: Exact endpoint/ROC/adjacent rational attainable interpolation

source_dispositions.text:
An arbitrary nonoptimal test need only have cost \emph{at least}
$\widetilde g(e)$ at its aggregated error $e$.  Equality is not asserted
for that aggregated record.  The following finer representation is what
preserves its continuation behavior.

\begin{lemma}[Record-level representation]
\label{lem:paid:representation}
In the cap-relaxed model, every finite-cost full-history policy is first
dominated by the policy that stops at permanent failure.  This dominated
policy can be simulated by symmetric integer boundary experiments and
private auxiliary records, preserving its virtual write-error,
correction, and abandonment history law up to termination, with no greater
expected review charge.  Conditional on an auxiliary writing record of
posterior level $m$, its mean review charge is $\mathsf C_m$, and its decision
error is either $p_m$ or $1-p_m$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Let $\pi_{\rm stop}$ be the input policy stopped at permanent failure.
It has the same success event and no greater cost than the input policy.
Condition on a generated virtual history before a fresh stage.  Let $Z$ be
the local record of $\pi_{\rm stop}$, containing its seed, observations, and
binary decision or abandonment label, but not a later truth report.
For analysis fill an unmade decision on abandonment; an unopened fact
has level zero.  Given a record $z$, let $m(z)$ be the magnitude of its
integer likelihood score and $s(z)$ its MAP orientation, with a fixed
tie convention.  The conditional truth distribution depends only on
this signed score: for a fixed record, the policy's sampling and
stopping factors do not depend on the hidden bit.

Sample $z$ from its original marginal law before observing the actual
fresh bit.  Run the symmetric level-$m(z)$ test and let $s'$ be its MAP
orientation.  Define the private coordinate flip $b=s(z)\mathbin\oplus s'$.
If $z$ writes $d(z)$, actually write $d(z)\mathbin\oplus b$.
After the actual report, the virtual truth $X\mathbin\oplus b$ differs
from $s(z)$ with probability exactly $p_{m(z)}$, conditional on $z$.
It therefore has the original posterior law.  The actual and virtual
write-error indicators agree.  Feed $z$ and this virtual report to the
old controller; genuine physical correction uses the actual mismatch
handle.  Future facts remain independent of this private virtual history.
Repeating the construction preserves the marked history law.

If the boundary test is also run on an auxiliary abandonment record, its
mean review charge satisfies
\[
 \E \mathsf C_{m(Z)}=a\E\phi(p_{m(Z)})=c\E T_{\rm stop}
                                      \le c\E T_{\rm input}.
\]
Alternatively copy that abandonment immediately and delete its
nonnegative testing charge; this gives the stated no-greater bound.
Thus record-level equality comes from stopped information, whereas an
aggregated-error projection supplies only the inequality in
Lemma~\ref{lem:paid:roc}.  Arbitrary trace laws can be sampled as probability
kernels; finite-cost truncation gives the same assertion at infima.
This is a comparison proof, not an efficient compiler for an unknown
policy.  The algorithm below needs no trace-distribution oracle.
\end{proof}
source_dispositions.summary: First-failure genuine record/history simulation and independent-inf identity

source_dispositions.text:
\begin{lemma}[A uniformly attainable local bound]
\label{lem:paid:surrogate}
For $0<p\le1/2$, put
\[
 \psi(p)=\max\{a\phi(p),(c/\gamma)(1/2-p)\}.
\]
Then $\psi(p)\le g(p)\le4\psi(p)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
On $[p_1,1/2]$, where $p_1=1/2-\gamma$, the first ROC chord is
$(c/\gamma)(1/2-p)$ and dominates $a\phi(p)$ by convexity.
For $p\le p_1$, writing $u=1/2-p$ gives
$a\phi(p)=(c/\gamma)u\log((1-p)/p)/h\ge(c/\gamma)u$.
If $p_{m+1}\le p\le p_m$ with $m\ge1$, concavity of $\tanh$ gives
\[
 \frac{\mathsf C_{m+1}}{\mathsf C_m}
 \le\left(\frac{m+1}{m}\right)^2\le4.
\]
Consequently $a\phi(p)\le g(p)\le \mathsf C_{m+1}\le4\mathsf C_m\le4a\phi(p)$.
\end{proof}
source_dispositions.summary: Original uniform surrogate and tiny-fee chord

source_dispositions.text:
\subsubsection{Survival information and actual correction usage}
\label{sec:paid:usage}

For $M>0$ and $x>0$, define
\[
 \mathcal H(M,x)=M\phi\!\left(\min\{1/2,x/M\}\right).
\]
It decreases in $x$ and increases in $M$.  In the positive region the
latter assertion follows from derivative
$\phi(q)-q\phi'(q)>0$, with $q=x/M$; in the remaining region it is zero.

\begin{lemma}[Actual-usage bound for current payment]
\label{lem:paid:usage}
For every native $\delta$-safe policy, if $r=\E R_{\rm act}$ and
$m=N(1-\delta)$, then
\begin{equation}
 \E C\ge a\mathcal H(m,r+\delta)+fr.
 \label{eq:paid:usage}
\end{equation}
The same inequality holds for finite-cost cap-relaxed policies.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For analysis stop at the first permanent failure or original abandonment,
retaining every earlier charge.  An erroneous output not corrected before
its current window closes is permanent failure.  Fill only a current
unmade decision by MAP.  An abandonment between stages is assigned to the
next required stage, if one remains, using a fresh analysis-only fair bit
with zero observations.  Do not fill all future stages.  No original
successful path is removed.

Let $A_i$ be eligibility for this truncated stage experiment, determined
before bit $i$ is born, and let $\mu_i=\Prob(A_i)$.  Every original
successful path enters every stage, so $\mu_i\ge1-\delta$.
Write $P_i$ for its posterior MAP error at its actual or filled stopping
point.  Lemma~\ref{lem:paid:information} gives
\begin{equation}
 \E C_{\rm obs}\ge
 a\sum_i\E[\ind_{A_i}\phi(P_i)].
 \label{eq:paid:surviving-information}
\end{equation}
This applies on pre-birth eligibility, not on eventual success.

An actual non-MAP decision has error at least its MAP error.  Each actual
or filled wrong decision in the truncated execution either receives an
actual correction or is assigned to the first failure/abandonment at
that stage.  These assigned failure events are disjoint.  Consequently
\begin{equation}
 b:=\sum_i\E[\ind_{A_i}P_i]\le r+\delta.
 \label{eq:paid:one-failure-allowance}
\end{equation}
The allowance is $\delta$, rather than $N\delta$, because only the current
abandoned decision was filled.  Corrections already executed on a later
failing path remain in $r$.

Let $M'=\sum_i\mu_i\ge m$.  Weighted Jensen in
\eqref{eq:paid:surviving-information} gives observation charge at least
$aM'\phi(b/M')$.  Its argument is at most $1/2$.
Monotonicity of $\mathcal H$ and
\eqref{eq:paid:one-failure-allowance} give
$a\mathcal H(M',b)\ge a\mathcal H(m,r+\delta)$.
Add the actual bill $fr$.  If the original policy spends after permanent
failure, the analysis removed only nonnegative observations and may keep
the larger original $r$; the bound remains valid.  Native finite quotas
justify stopped summation directly.  In the relaxed model finite expected
cost gives integrability; infinite-cost policies need no bound.
\end{proof}
source_dispositions.summary: Prebirth survival/single fill, true actual payment allowance, Jensen and fees

source_dispositions.text:
\begin{lemma}[Uniform fee scale]
\label{lem:paid:fee-scale}
Every $\delta$-safe current-payment policy satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \E C\ge\frac{aN}{128}
       \log\left(1+\min\{f/a,N/\delta\}\right).
 \label{eq:paid:fee-scale}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The case $f=0$ is immediate.  Put $u=f/a$, $d=\delta/m\le1/63$,
and $w=\min\{u,1/d\}$.  If $(r+\delta)/m\ge1/2$, the fee term divided
by $am$ is at least $u(1/2-d)$, which is at least
$\log(1+w)/64$.  Otherwise put $p=(r+\delta)/m\in[d,1/2]$.
The normalized right side of \eqref{eq:paid:usage} is
$\phi(p)+u(p-d)$.

If $w<16$ and $p\le1/4$, then
$\phi(p)\ge\phi(1/4)=(\log3)/2>\log17/64$.
If $w<16$ and $p>1/4$, then $p-d>1/5$, so
$u(p-d)\ge w/5\ge\log(1+w)/5$.
If $w\ge16$ and $p\le1/\sqrt w$, then
\[
 \phi(p)\ge\tfrac14\log w+\tfrac12\log(3/4)
            \ge\tfrac1{64}\log(1+w).
\]
The last inequality holds at $w=16$, and its left-minus-right derivative
is positive thereafter.  In the remaining case $w\ge16$ and
$p>1/\sqrt w$, use $d\le1/w$ and $u\ge w$ to get
$u(p-d)\ge\sqrt w-1\ge\log(1+w)/64$.

Thus \eqref{eq:paid:usage} is at least
$(am/64)\log(1+\min\{u,m/\delta\})$.
Write $m=\beta N$ with $\beta\ge63/64$.
The inequalities
$\min\{u,\beta x\}\ge\beta\min\{u,x\}$ and
$\log(1+\beta z)\ge\beta\log(1+z)$ lose at most $\beta^2$ when
replacing $m$ by $N$.  Since $\beta^2/64\ge1/128$, the result follows.
\end{proof}

The execution requirement in Lemma~\ref{lem:paid:usage} is essential.
If unpaid obligations may be retained, a wrong output on a failing path
need not ever incur a correction charge.  Section~\ref{sec:paid:payment-limit}
gives a low-risk counterexample to transferring
\eqref{eq:paid:one-failure-allowance} to that permission.
source_dispositions.summary: Uniform exact fee lower and payment permission boundary

source_dispositions.text:
\subsubsection{A paid simulation that preserves task risk}
\label{sec:paid:overlay}

The next theorem is a cap-relaxed comparison.  Its simulator is not
asserted to preserve a given native stopping-time bound.

\begin{theorem}[Paid overlay]
\label{thm:paid:overlay}
For every finite-cost free-correction policy $\pi_0$, there is a
current-payment policy $\pi_f$ with no larger failure probability and
\begin{equation}
 \E C(\pi_f)\le\E C_{\rm obs}(\pi_0)
       +\tfrac{17}{2}Na\log(1+f/a).
 \label{eq:paid:overlay-policy}
\end{equation}
In particular
\begin{equation}
 V_f^\infty(\delta)\le V_0^\infty(\delta)+9D_f.
 \label{eq:paid:overlay-value}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Put $u=f/a$ and $p_f=1/[2(1+u)]$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 fp_f=\frac a2\frac{u}{1+u}
       \le\frac a2\log(1+u).
 \label{eq:paid:weighted-correction}
\end{equation}
At this target,
\[
 \phi(p_f)=\frac{u}{1+u}\log(1+2u)\le2\log(1+u),
 \qquad
 \frac c\gamma(1/2-p_f)=ah\frac{u}{1+u}
                         \le ah\log(1+u).
\]
As $h\le\log3<2$, Lemma~\ref{lem:paid:surrogate} implies
\begin{equation}
 g(p_f)\le8a\log(1+u).
 \label{eq:paid:overlay-local}
\end{equation}
The linear first-chord term in that lemma controls arbitrarily small
$u$; a large-penalty logarithmic approximation would not suffice there.

First stop the input free policy at permanent failure; this preserves
its success event and does not increase its charge.  Apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:paid:representation} to this dominated policy.  Conditional on
an auxiliary writing record $z$, let $p=p_{m(z)}$ be its MAP error and
$d(z)$ its virtual output.  Its conditional decision error is $e=p$ if
that decision is MAP and $e=1-p$ otherwise.  In both cases $e\ge p$.
Copy a virtual abandonment, deleting nonnegative work.

For a writing record, run an actual MAP experiment of exact error
$p'=\min\{p,p_f\}$.  After its real report let $E'$ be the actual error.
If $E'=1$, declare the virtual error $E=1$.  If $E'=0$, declare $E=1$
with probability
\begin{equation}
 \frac{e-p'}{1-p'}.
 \label{eq:paid:false-positive-virtual-error}
\end{equation}
This is a valid probability.  It gives $\Prob(E=1\mid z)=e$ and
$E'\le E$ pathwise.  Feed the virtual truth $d(z)\mathbin\oplus E$ to
the old controller.  Conditional on $z$ this truth has exactly its
original posterior law, even for a non-MAP output.  Therefore the virtual
controller reproduces the dominated stopped free policy's marked history
up to termination.  That policy has no greater charge and the same
success event as the input free policy.
Freshness makes that old virtual history legitimate private state before
each next fact; no future truth is inspected.

Whenever the virtual controller allocates a correction, reserve that
right in its ledger.  On an actual error, immediately perform its
genuine correction using the actual mismatch handle and pay $f$.
On a virtual false positive, make no physical correction and only
discard the virtual right.  A virtually unused tool is physically
unused, since actual errors are a subset of virtual errors.  Hence at
most $K$ real corrections occur.  If the old policy refuses a necessary
correction or abandons, the simulator may abandon as well.  Every virtual
successful path is an actual successful path, proving the risk claim.
The virtual reports authorize no native call; only actual handles do.

The old writing-record review charge is $g(p)=\mathsf C_m$.
If $p\le p_f$, the new charge is unchanged.  Otherwise its increase is
at most $g(p_f)$, since $g(p)\ge0$.  At each visited stage the actual
correction probability is at most $p'\le p_f$.  Summing
\eqref{eq:paid:weighted-correction} and \eqref{eq:paid:overlay-local} over at most
$N$ stages proves \eqref{eq:paid:overlay-policy}.  When $u=0$ there is no
increase.  Taking infima proves \eqref{eq:paid:overlay-value}.
\end{proof}

This existence comparison uses the distribution of a supplied free
policy only in its proof.  The rational algorithm in the next section
neither receives an optimal free controller nor executes this trace
simulation under a hard quota.
source_dispositions.summary: Actual paid overlay/history/error/physical fee laws
Original actual native eight-factor algorithm

source_dispositions.text:
\paragraph{Exact penalty programs and a derived finite menu}

For a failure penalty $\lambda\ge0$, let $F_{n,k}(\lambda)$ be the
cap-relaxed infimum of expected variable charge plus
$\lambda\Prob(\mathrm{failure})$, from $n$ fresh facts and $k$ tools.
Set $F_{0,k}=0$.  At a nonterminal state define
\begin{equation}
 A_{n,k}=F_{n-1,k},\qquad
 B_{n,k}=\begin{cases}
 \lambda,&k=0,\\
 \min\{\lambda,f+F_{n-1,k-1}\},&k>0.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:paid:paid-successors}
\end{equation}
More tools cannot hurt, so $0\le A_{n,k}\le B_{n,k}\le\lambda$.
The exact program is
\begin{equation}
 F_{n,k}=\min\left\{\lambda,
 \min_{m\ge0}\bigl[\mathsf C_m+(1-p_m)A_{n,k}+p_m B_{n,k}\bigr]\right\}.
 \label{eq:paid:exact-penalty-program}
\end{equation}
The bad-branch minimum records actual correction and payment or
abandonment before payment.

For completeness this program bounds the full history class.  Condition
on any generated past before a fresh bit.  Its actual local write is an
arbitrary sequential binary decision.  Correct and erroneous
continuations have lower bounds $A_{n,k}$ and $B_{n,k}$ regardless of
the old transcript or private seed.  As their difference is nonnegative,
MAP can only lower this local comparison.  Lemma~\ref{lem:paid:roc} gives
the inner minimization, attained at a ROC endpoint since the local
objective is linear on every chord.  If the original policy abandons
during a test, keep its already-bought observations and fill a binary
decision for analysis.  Both virtual continuations are at most
$\lambda$, so this cannot increase the comparison.  Spending after
permanent failure is nonnegative.  Backward induction proves the lower
bound, and the displayed tests and continuation choices implement its
right side.  Thus \eqref{eq:paid:exact-penalty-program} is exact without
restricting the comparator to Markov or MAP policies.
source_dispositions.summary: Independent full-policy paid Bellman, actual payment and near-inf continuation

source_dispositions.text:
Choose the smallest minimizing testing index.  A finite minimizer exists
because $\mathsf C_m\to\infty$.  If $D=B_{n,k}-A_{n,k}$ and this index $m\ge1$,
then
\[
 \mathsf C_m+Dp_m<\mathsf C_{m-1}+Dp_{m-1}.
\]
On the same observation tape the level-$m$ hitting test needs at least
one more observation after the level-$(m-1)$ hitting time.  Therefore
$\mathsf C_m-\mathsf C_{m-1}\ge c$, and
\begin{equation}
 Dp_{m-1}>c.
 \label{eq:paid:menu-necessary}
\end{equation}
If $0\le\lambda\le\Lambda$ and $m>M$, then
$Dp_{m-1}\le\Lambda p_M\le c$, a contradiction.
Consequently indices $0,\ldots,M$ suffice for every queried multiplier.
Minimality of $M$ gives
\begin{equation}
 p_M\ge p_{M-1}/R>c/(3\Lambda)=\varepsilon,
 \label{eq:paid:menu-floor}
\end{equation}
since $R\le3$.  Here $\Lambda>2c$, so $M\ge1$.
This is a derived menu, not an assumed floor for an unknown optimum.
All its coordinates \eqref{eq:paid:roc-points} are rational.
source_dispositions.summary: Least endpoint, original finite menu and fee-independent floor

source_dispositions.text:
Each table entry stores its selected action, expected observation charge,
expected actual correction count, and failure probability.  Their
recursions use the same weights $1-p_m,p_m$; current review charge is
$\mathsf C_m$ and a chosen correction adds one actual call.  Correlation of a
test's duration with its error does not invalidate these mean recursions:
the future chosen policies ignore that duration and freshness fixes their
conditional values.
source_dispositions.summary: True actual menu means/guard rather than table bookkeeping

source_dispositions.text:
\paragraph{Two-policy calibration and a finite stopping rule}

The $t_0$-majority baseline in \eqref{eq:paid:certificate-numbers} has risk at
most $\delta/2$ by the BSC Chernoff bound and costs $B$.  It is used here
only in the cap-relaxed comparison.  Hence an optimal policy at
$\lambda=\Lambda$ has risk
\[
 r_U\le F_{N,K}(\Lambda)/\Lambda
       \le B/\Lambda+\delta/2=3\delta/4.
\]
At multiplier zero choose immediate abandonment of risk one and cost zero.
Maintain two exactly optimal endpoint policies with
$\lambda_L<\lambda_U$, risks $r_L>\delta\ge r_U$, and mean actual
costs $C_L,C_U$.  Bisect the multiplier interval and update the endpoint
according to its computed risk.  An optimal policy of risk exactly
$\delta$ can be returned immediately: its cost is
$F_{N,K}(\lambda)-\lambda\delta\le V_f^\infty(\delta)$ by weak duality,
and feasibility gives the reverse inequality.  Otherwise mix the endpoint
policies at the beginning with weight
\begin{equation}
 w=\frac{\delta-r_U}{r_L-r_U}
 \label{eq:paid:initial-mixture}
\end{equation}
on the lower endpoint.  Its risk is exactly $\delta$ and its mean cost
is $U=wC_L+(1-w)C_U$.

Let $L=F_{N,K}(\lambda_U)-\lambda_U\delta$.
Endpoint optimality gives
\[
 -\lambda_U\le\frac{C_L-C_U}{r_L-r_U}\le-\lambda_L.
\]
Thus, directly rather than by subtracting unrelated multiplicative
approximations,
\begin{equation}
 0\le U-L\le(\lambda_U-\lambda_L)(\delta-r_U)
                \le(\lambda_U-\lambda_L)\delta.
 \label{eq:paid:mixture-gap}
\end{equation}
Weak duality alone gives $L\le V_f^\infty(\delta)\le U$.
Stop when the rightmost expression is at most $U/2$; then
\begin{equation}
 U\le2V_f^\infty(\delta).
 \label{eq:paid:two-factor-reference}
\end{equation}
No infinite-policy strong-duality theorem is needed.
source_dispositions.summary: Real majority bracket, initial whole-policy mixture, same-risk gap/weak dual

source_dispositions.text:
There is an explicit termination bound even near zero value.  The
minimum risk with zero variable charges is
\begin{equation}
 \zeta_f=\begin{cases}
 \Prob\{\operatorname{Bin}(N,1/2)>K\},&f=0,\\
 1-2^{-N},&f>0.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:paid:zero-charge-risk}
\end{equation}
Without reviews every next predictable guess has independent error
$1/2$.  If $f=0$, at most $K$ such errors are repairable; if $f>0$, a
zero-charge policy cannot execute a correction, so it must guess all bits
correctly.  Filling unvisited guesses after abandonment proves these
lower bounds, and the corresponding blind policies attain them.
If $\delta\ge\zeta_f$, return that zero-cost native policy.

Otherwise let $b_f=c$ for $f=0$ and $b_f=\min\{c,f\}$ for $f>0$, and put
$\ell=b_f(\zeta_f-\delta)>0$.
Every $\delta$-safe policy costs at least $\ell$.
Indeed keep its behavior until just before its first positive-charge
operation, then replace the remainder by a zero-charge continuation.
This causal policy has risk at least $\zeta_f$ and can change failure
only on the event of that operation.  That event has probability at
least $\zeta_f-\delta$, and the old bill is at least $b_f$ there.
This argument also applies to cap-relaxed policies.
Consequently $U\ge\ell$, and at most
\begin{equation}
 J_{\rm bis}=\max\left\{0,
       \left\lceil\log_2\frac{2\Lambda\delta}{\ell}\right\rceil\right\}
 \label{eq:paid:bisection-count}
\end{equation}
bisections suffice for \eqref{eq:paid:two-factor-reference}.
source_dispositions.summary: All-seed zero charge, causal first-positive floor and true bounded bisection

source_dispositions.text:
\paragraph{Bounded tests with exactly the same errors}

An endpoint policy still has unbounded review durations.  We now replace
each endpoint experiment by a bounded one without increasing its risk.
For $m=0$ write blindly.  For $1\le m\le M$, run the symmetric
level-$(m+1)$ test for at most $Q$ reviews, then write MAP, randomizing a
tie.  Call its actual error $q_m$.

Conditional on either truth, the unrestricted true-direction score has
increments of mean $\kappa$ in an interval of length $2h$.
On nonexit at time $Q$ its score is below $(m+1)h$.
Since $Q\ge(M+1)/\gamma=2(M+1)h/\kappa$, Hoeffding gives
\begin{equation}
 \Prob(T_{m+1}>Q)\le e^{-\gamma^2Q/2}
       \le e^{-E}\le2^{-E}\le\gamma\varepsilon.
 \label{eq:paid:bounded-tail}
\end{equation}
The logistic formula and \eqref{eq:paid:menu-floor} give
\[
 p_{m+1}\le(1-2\gamma)p_m,
 \qquad q_m\le p_{m+1}+\gamma\varepsilon
                   \le p_m-\gamma\varepsilon<p_m.
\]
Compute $q_m$ exactly with a length-$Q$ rational random-walk table,
absorbing at $\pm(m+1)$ and applying its terminal MAP/tie decision.
source_dispositions.summary: Original finite walk/capped endpoint/error and tail
Literal rational exact calibration for each truth and local cost4

source_dispositions.text:
Ignore excess actual test details and follow the stored endpoint policy.
At every entry its conditional error probability is still exactly $p_m$,
so the complete error, correction-choice and failure law is unchanged.
Actual correction fees have exactly their old distribution, including
payments before eventual failure.  Nonnegativity therefore yields
\[
 \E C_{\rm bounded}\le4U\le8V_f^\infty(\delta).
\]
Every path uses at most $NQ$ reviews, $H_0$ normal calls, and $K$ actual
corrections.  The initial mixture selects one whole lawful policy and
does not add resource usage across its branches.  Qualification
\eqref{eq:paid:cap-certificate} proves native feasibility, finishing
Theorem~\ref{thm:paid:native-eight}.
source_dispositions.summary: WHOLE discrete/actual correction fee law and native8 migration

source_dispositions.text:
\paragraph{Explicit computation and bit lengths}

One penalty solve uses $O(N(K+1)(M+1))$ rational operations and
$O(N(K+1))$ stored actions and mean-value records.  There are at most
$J_{\rm bis}+2$ solves.  The calibration uses
$O(Q(M+1)^2)$ rational updates, summing the widths of the separate
birth--death walks; it is done once.  Thus the output is compact in these
displayed numerical parameters, with no exponential history tree.

Let $L$ bound the bit length of menu probabilities, menu costs, and input
fees.  The product of their denominators has $O((M+1)L)$ bits.
Depth-$N$ policy probabilities and mean costs have denominator bit length
$O((N+1)(M+1)L)$, with multiplier bits added for penalty objectives.
Numerators additionally count value magnitudes and the bit lengths of
$N,K$.  The calibration denominator has $O(Q L_\gamma)$ bits, where
$L_\gamma$ is the channel input length.  Initial mixture probabilities
add endpoint and $\delta$ bit lengths.  Subtracting rational endpoint
risks does not introduce an exponential number of bits.

The positive difference $\zeta_f-\delta$ is at least the reciprocal of
$2^N$ times the denominator of $\delta$; hence
$\log(1/(\zeta_f-\delta))=O(N+L_\delta)$ when it is positive.
The bit length of a very small positive $f$ is counted in $b_f$.
For fixed rational $\gamma$, $t_0,M,Q,J_{\rm bis}$ and the foregoing bit
costs are polynomial in explicit $N$ and remaining input lengths.
For variable-precision $\gamma$, dependence on numerical $1/\gamma$ is
displayed; polynomial dependence on $\log(1/\gamma)$ is not asserted.
Exact rational coins can be sampled with ordinary private randomness;
they consume no native observation or correction call.
source_dispositions.summary: Actual full program phases/time/space/operand bits/raw-input TM and exact private sampling

\subsubsection{Proof of the price separation}
\label{sec:paid:separation}

\begin{lemma}[No-correction comparison]
\label{lem:paid:no-correction}
In the cap-relaxed model,
$V_f^\infty(\delta)\le7S_\delta$ for every $f\ge0$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
At every stage take the least positive odd number $t$ of reviews such that
$(1-4\gamma^2)^t\le(\delta/N)^2$, and write its majority.
The BSC Chernoff bound gives each error at most $\delta/N$; a union bound
makes the task $\delta$-safe without any correction.
Odd rounding and $-\log(1-4\gamma^2)\ge4\gamma^2$ give
\[
 t\le\frac{\log(N/\delta)}{2\gamma^2}+2.
\]
From $h=2\operatorname{arctanh}(2\gamma)$,
\[
 8\gamma^2\le\kappa\le\frac{32}{3}\gamma^2.
\]
Since $N/\delta\ge64$, these inequalities imply
$ct\le7a\log(N/\delta)$ with slack.  All reviews are charged, including
those on failing paths.  The total is at most
$7aN\log(N/\delta)\le7S_\delta$.
This is a relaxed comparison; under native caps it would separately
require $t$ reviews per stage.  We use
Theorem~\ref{thm:paid:native-eight} to implement the resulting value comparison
under the different, explicit certificate \eqref{eq:paid:cap-certificate}.
\end{proof}
source_dispositions.summary: True no-correction all-path majority and original7S relaxed witness

source_dispositions.text:
\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:paid:separation}]
Its algorithmic assertion is Theorem~\ref{thm:paid:native-eight}.
Let $A_\infty=V_0^\infty(\delta)\le A$.
Theorem~\ref{thm:paid:overlay} and Lemma~\ref{lem:paid:no-correction} give
\[
 V_f^\infty(\delta)\le
       \min\{A_\infty+9D_f,7S_\delta\}.
\]
The native algorithm is feasible in the original paid instance and yields
\[
 V_f^{\rm nat}(\delta)
 \le8\min\{A_\infty+9D_f,7S_\delta\}
 \le72\min\{A+D_f,S_\delta\}=72T.
\]
This step does not execute an unbounded free-policy overlay under a hard
quota.  Its native execution is supplied by the independent cap bridge.

For the lower bound, setting $f$ to zero changes no legal action, tool
right, quota, or call count, since there is no monetary cap.  The risk
is unchanged and the charge decreases, so
$V_f^{\rm nat}(\delta)\ge A$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:paid:fee-scale} gives the additional necessary expenditure
\[
 V_f^{\rm nat}(\delta)\ge\frac{\min\{D_f,S_\delta\}}{128}.
\]
For $b=\min\{D_f,S_\delta\}$, one has $T\le A+b$ and
$\max\{A,b/128\}\ge(A+b)/129$.  Taking the larger lower bound,
rather than charging their review components twice, proves
$V_f^{\rm nat}(\delta)\ge T/129$.
\end{proof}
source_dispositions.summary: Same-native129/72 and real native8, preserving comparison rights

source_dispositions.text:
Without native caps, the same argument gives the related comparison
\[
 \frac1{129}\min\{A_\infty+D_f,S_\delta\}
 \le V_f^\infty(\delta)
 \le9\min\{A_\infty+D_f,S_\delta\}.
\]
The same-native statement is stronger than replacing $A$ by an
uncontrolled capped-versus-uncapped surrogate: its lower side uses the
actual original free instance directly, and its upper side uses a
certificate independent of the price.

\subsubsection{Why delayed unpaid obligations require a different bound}
\label{sec:paid:payment-limit}

Suppose a retained-payment contract permits all correction obligations to
remain unpaid until a final barrier.  Consider zero review quotas,
$K=N-1$, $\delta=2^{-N}$, and $N\ge6$.  Guess all bits blindly and,
with $Z\sim\operatorname{Bin}(N,1/2)$, correct exactly its $Z$ errors
when $Z<N$; abandon without correction payment when $Z=N$.
This has the minimum blind risk and expected correction count
\[
 r=N/2-N\delta.
\]
All $N$ posterior MAP errors equal $1/2$, but
$r+\delta=N/2-(N-1)\delta<N(1-\delta)/2$ for $N>2$.
Applying \eqref{eq:paid:usage} would then assert a strictly positive review
charge, although the policy buys none.  The successful-path correction
requirement alone therefore does not prove our current-payment usage
inequality.  An irrevocable assignment whose payment can still be
withheld on abandonment has this same financial issue.


This is a counterexample to transferring the actual-usage inequality,
not an impossibility theorem for every price-separation formula with
retained payment.  It also does not invalidate the main fixed-fee
structural law, whose comparison and asymptotic regime are different.
source_dispositions.summary: Genuine native delayed-payment usage counterexample, not universal impossibility
